summary: A character the server spawns and owns. The nearest player's game within 150 m simulates its body, including movement, pathfinding and fights, and other games show what that one reports. The server holds its health, inventory and orders, so all players see the same NPC. Orders such as moveTo, follow, flee, patrol and attack use the game's movement and pathfinding.

create.summary: Spawns an NPC. By default it is vulnerable, lootable, at full health, and in its soul's clothes.

params.options: `position`, required; `soul`, a role from Npc.roles() or a soul GUID from the game's tables; `class`, 'NPC', 'NPC_Female' or an animal class, where a role picks the right body; `name`; `rotation`; `dimension`; `map`, one of World.maps, the first by default; `frozen`; `appearance`, as for setAppearance; `health`; `invulnerable`; `lootable`; `outfit`, a preset as for setOutfit; `wearing`, item classes; `nameplate`, true draws its name over it, off by default; `locomotion`, 'native' or 'kinematic'; `faction`, a faction row, 0 for none; `brain`, false means the game's brain never starts; `interactable`, false gives no use prompt from the start; `nameShown`, false leaves its name out of the HUD's corner from the start; `targetable`, false gives no lock-on; `fightsBack`, false takes blows without fighting back. With `brain: false` and `interactable: false`, it is a mannequin from its first frame on all clients.

create.exampleLua:
local guard = kcds.characters.Npc.create({ soul = "guard", name = "Gate guard", nameplate = true, position = kcds.math.Vector3.new(2340, 2070, 110) })
guard:setNameplateText("Town guard")
guard:lookAt(player)
guard:say("Halt! Who goes there?")

all.summary: All NPCs, or those in one dimension.

params.dimension: Optional: limits it to this dimension.

all.exampleLua:
local Npc = kcds.characters.Npc

for _, npc in ipairs(Npc.all()) do
  print(npc.name .. " (" .. tostring(npc.id) .. ") at " .. tostring(npc.position))
end
local inArena = Npc.all(7)

getById.summary: The NPC with this network id, or null.
getById.exampleLua:
kcds.core.Events.fromClient("npc:hail", function(player, payload)
  local npc = kcds.characters.Npc.getById(tonumber((payload and payload.id)))
  if npc and npc.alive then
    npc:lookAt(player)
  end
end)

removeAll.summary: Removes all NPCs, or those in one dimension, and returns how many.

params.dimension: Optional: limits it to this dimension.

name.summary: Its name. You can assign to it, and nearby players see the new name.

animals.summary: Animals from the population, living and dead, as Npc objects. They belong to no resource and stay when a resource stops.

placedGuid.summary: Always 0, since a scripted NPC is not one of the level's.

soul.summary: The game soul it was created from, which gives its character, skills and look.

actorClass.summary: Its actor class in the game.
actorClass.exampleLua:
if npc.actorClass == "NPC_Female" then
  print("a woman")
end

health.summary: Its health, 0 to 100. Setting 0 kills it, firing npcDeath with no killer, and more than maxHealth is limited to it.

alive.exampleLua:
local living = {}
for _, npc in ipairs(kcds.characters.Npc.all()) do
  if npc.alive then
    table.insert(living, npc)
  end
end

frozen.summary: While true, it stays where it is and keeps its order. You can assign to it.
frozen.exampleLua:
npc.frozen = true
setTimeout(function()
  npc.frozen = false
end, 5000)

map.summary: The map it stands on, one of World.maps, as Npc.create placed it. Players on another map never see it, and it never fights them.
map.example:
const guards = kcds.characters.Npc.all().filter((npc) => npc.map === 'kutnohorsko');
console.info(`${guards.length} NPCs in Kuttenberg`);
map.exampleLua:
local count = 0
for _, npc in ipairs(kcds.characters.Npc.all()) do
  if npc.map == "kutnohorsko" then
    count = count + 1
  end
end
print(count .. " NPCs in Kuttenberg")
map.exampleCs:
var guards = Npc.All().Count(npc => npc.Map == "kutnohorsko");
Log.Info($"{guards} NPCs in Kuttenberg");

dimension.summary: Its dimension. Change it with setDimension.
dimension.exampleLua:
if npc.dimension == player.dimension then
  npc:lookAt(player)
end

rotation.summary: The direction it faces. Assigning turns it.

setDimension.summary: Moves it to another dimension, where only players there see it.

showOnlyTo.summary: Lets one player see it even outside its dimension, or nobody extra with null.

setAppearance.summary: Gives it other character parts, with names from Appearances.options for its gender. Parts left out stay, and '' restores the soul's. Returns false for an unknown name, or a beard the face cannot have.

damage.summary: Takes health as a scripted hit, firing npcDamage, and npcDeath if none is left. Returns false for a dead, invulnerable or gone NPC.

params.attacker: Optional: a Player, a player's id, an Npc, or null.

kill.summary: Kills it with the game's death, firing npcDeath. Returns false for a dead or gone NPC.

params.killer: Optional: who is named as the killer.

revive.summary: Brings back a dead NPC where it lies, firing npcRevive. Returns false for a living or gone NPC.

routeState.summary: Its patrol, { routeId, waypointIndex, lap, direction, phase }, or null if not patrolling.
routeState.exampleLua:
local patrol = npc.routeState
if patrol then
  print("waypoint " .. tostring(patrol.waypointIndex) .. ", lap " .. tostring(patrol.lap))
end

playAnimation.summary: Plays a Mannequin fragment with tags, as for a player, or a game clip. Nearby players see it, and so does a player arriving later or simulating it next, until stopAnimation or the next playAnimation. npcAnimationEnd reports how it ended: 'finished', 'interrupted', 'refused', 'stopped' or 'replaced'. Returns true when the request goes out.

params.fragment: The fragment's name, such as 'Greetings', or '' with a clip. A name the body lacks ends at once as 'refused'.
params.options: `tags`, separated by '+', such as 'bowBig'; `clip`, by name or path, instead of the fragment; `loop`, which repeats until stopAnimation or the next playAnimation.

playAnimation.exampleLua:
guard:hold()
guard:playAnimation("Greetings", { tags = "bowBig" })

kcds.core.Events.on("npcAnimationEnd", function(npc, fragment, reason)
  if npc ~= guard then
    return
  end
  print(fragment .. " ended: " .. tostring(reason))
  if fragment == "Greetings" then
    guard:playAnimation("", { clip = "reading_stand_inv_in", loop = true })
  end
end)

stopAnimation.summary: Ends what playAnimation started at once and returns the body to its order, and npcAnimationEnd says 'stopped'. Returns true when the request goes out.

adopt.summary: Gives one of the level's people to a script, as a server NPC at the level's position for them. The body stays when players leave, and the same GUID again gives the same NPC, without applying the options again. Null if the GUID is not in the level. Throws a TypeError for unusable arguments.

params.placedGuid: The guid from Npc.placements, with or without 0x.
params.options: Optional: as for Npc.create, with `soul` being the placement's.

adopt.exampleLua:
local Npc = kcds.characters.Npc

local first = table.unpack(Npc.placements())
local gerta = (first and Npc.adopt(first.guid, { name = "Gerta" }) or nil)
if gerta then
  gerta:say("Good day.")
end

setPopulation.summary: Settings for the level's people, on by default. All players see the same ones, spawned around players at the level's positions. They walk a relaxed round of neighbouring places, a patrol scripts can replace with any order. They do not follow the level's schedules, and those a quest stages are left out, though Npc.adopt can still get them. Players cannot talk to them: they are not interactable, and a script can set interactable to true on one it adopts. people-population.json in the resources folder sets the same. Throws a RangeError or TypeError for an unusable value.

params.settings: `enabled`, default true; `activationRadius`, metres from a player, default 80; `despawnRadius`, default 120, at least activationRadius; `maxPeople`, default 48, 0 to 512; `share`, the percent of the level's people who get bodies, 0 to 100, default 100: the same ones for every player and every start, and a smaller share only takes people away (not with levelPeople).

setPopulation.exampleLua:
local Npc = kcds.characters.Npc

Npc.setPopulation({ maxPeople = 24, activationRadius = 60, despawnRadius = 90 })
Npc.setPopulation({ share = 50 }) -- half of the level's people
Npc.setPopulation({ enabled = false })

placements.summary: The level's people as it places them, on the server's level: { name, guid, level, layer, soul, actorClass, position, rotation }. These are their first positions, not where a schedule or quest has them. It spawns nothing, so a script can build its own population from them.
placements.exampleLua:
local Npc = kcds.characters.Npc

for _, row in ipairs(Npc.placements()) do
  if string.find(row.name, "smith", 1, true) then
    Npc.create({ soul = row.soul, position = row.position })
  end
end

lootOf.summary: The game's loot candidates for this animal, by soul. It rolls nothing and fills nothing, so the script chooses and writes the carcass's inventory. Each row is { item (class GUID), name, amount (the most units), fraction and variation (the game's share and spread, not a drop chance), food, harvester (a special_ part or trophy) }. Null for a body that is not an animal with a game preset, including wild dogs.
lootOf.exampleLua:
local boar = kcds.characters.Npc.create({ position = { x = 1200, y = 800, z = 40 }, class = "Boar" })
local loot = boar:lootOf()
if loot then
  local food = {}
  for _, row in ipairs(loot) do
    if row.food then
      table.insert(food, row.name)
    end
  end
  print(table.concat(food, ", "))
end

setExpression.summary: Changes its expression for all clients, including later joiners, alongside body animations. It affects eyes, brows and mood, so use setSpeaking for the mouth. Returns true once sent, and false for a dead NPC. Invalid arguments throw a TypeError.

params.fragment: FE_Default, FE_DialogueIdle or FE_DialogueSpeaking, or '' to return the face to the game.
params.options: Optional: `tags` sets the mood: happy, angry, sad, nervous, pensive, arogant or drunk.

setSpeaking.summary: Starts a repeating talking animation from the game's face clips until stopped, for all clients including later joiners. It is not lip-sync, so use it with say. Returns true once sent, and false for a dead NPC. An unknown style throws a TypeError.

params.talking: True to move the mouth, false to stop.
params.style: Optional: neutral (default), happy, drunk or chew.

say.summary: Shows text in the game's speech bubble over its head for nearby players. '' removes it.

params.options: Optional: `duration` in milliseconds. By default, longer text stays longer.

say.exampleCs: npc.Say("Halt! Who goes there?", new { duration = 4000 });

playVoice.summary: Server only. Plays a voice line from its body for the players near it, as each one's client would with Audio.playFile: one of the game's own lines under Localization/dialog/, or a resource's .ogg. The line is told once: a player who comes near later does not hear it. Returns whether any player was told. Throws a TypeError for a path that is not a game-root path and a RangeError for an unknown purpose.

params.file: A game-root path with forward slashes, such as Localization/dialog/<line>, without a drive or parent folder.
params.options: Optional: `purpose`, the game's voice event: 'inner', '10', '20', '35', '50' (default), '100' or '200', heard up to that many metres, or 'sfp_dialog', 'sfp_cutscene' or 'sfp_music'; `range`, the players told, in metres up to 200, by default the purpose's distance (30 for the others).

playVoice.example:
// The smith greets whoever is near, in the game's own voice.
smith.playVoice('Localization/dialog/smith_greeting_01', { purpose: '20' });
playVoice.exampleLua:
-- The smith greets whoever is near, in the game's own voice.
smith:playVoice("Localization/dialog/smith_greeting_01", { purpose = "20" })
playVoice.exampleCs:
// The smith greets whoever is near, in the game's own voice.
smith.PlayVoice("Localization/dialog/smith_greeting_01", new { purpose = "20" });

roles.summary: The named kinds of NPC: guard, guard_alt, knight, bandit, bandit_alt, cuman, townsman, townsman_alt, townswoman and townswoman_alt. Each maps to a soul from the game's data, giving a suitable look and gender. Pass the name as `soul` to Npc.create, where other values must be a soul GUID.
roles.exampleLua:
local Npc = kcds.characters.Npc

local roles = Npc.roles()
local role = roles[math.floor(math.random() * #roles) + 1]
Npc.create({ soul = role, position = player.position })

nameplate.summary: Whether its name is drawn over its head for all players, as for a player, with the name or setNameplateText's text, and a health bar below. Off by default. Any player can still turn plates off on their own screen with the client's Nameplates.
nameplate.example: const smith = kcds.characters.Npc.create({ soul: 'townsman', name: 'Smith', nameplate: true, position });
nameplate.exampleLua: local smith = kcds.characters.Npc.create({ soul = "townsman", name = "Smith", nameplate = true, position = position })
nameplate.exampleCs: var smith = Npc.Create(new { soul = "townsman", name = "Smith", nameplate = true, position = position });

isNameplateVisible.summary: Whether its plate is drawn, the same switch as `nameplate`. False by default.

setNameplateVisible.summary: Shows or hides its plate for all players, the same switch as `nameplate`.

isNameplateHealthVisible.summary: Whether the health bar shows. True by default.

setNameplateHealthVisible.summary: Turns the health bar on or off, while the name stays.

getNameplateText.summary: The text drawn in place of its name, or '' while the name is drawn.

setNameplateText.summary: Sets the plate's text, up to 64 UTF-8 bytes on one line. Its real `name` stays, and is still used for conversation and its soul.

params.text: The text. '' or nothing draws the name again.

getNameplateColor.summary: The plate text's colour as 0xAARRGGBB, opaque white unless tinted.

locomotion.summary: How the simulating game moves the body for moveTo, follow, flee and patrol. 'native', the default, walks it with the game's movement and animations. A hen's default is 'kinematic', because the game's own walk takes a hen its own way. 'kinematic' moves it along the way at the order's pace, on the ground and facing its direction, with no walking animations. Neither finds a way around obstacles by itself. Only these two strings are accepted, and anything else throws.
locomotion.exampleLua:
-- A cart driver sliding along the road.
driver.locomotion = "kinematic"
driver:moveTo(kcds.math.Vector3.new(2346, 2078, 110), { speed = "jog" })

faction.summary: The faction row your resource gave it, or 0: a whole number from 0 to 65535 the server keeps for your scripts. The body currently keeps its soul's faction in the game.

pin.summary: Lets one player's game run it regardless of distance, for a scene played to that player. While pinned, it goes dormant when that player is out of range, rather than moving to someone else, and it unpins when they leave the server.

params.player: A Player or player id. null returns control to the closest player.

pin.exampleLua:
local actor = kcds.characters.Npc.create({ soul = "townswoman", position = stage })
actor:pin(player)

-- After the scene:
actor:pin(null)

pinnedTo.summary: The player it is pinned to, or null.
pinnedTo.exampleLua:
if npc.pinnedTo then
  print(tostring(npc.name) .. " is simulated by " .. tostring(npc.pinnedTo.nickname))
end

setAnimalPopulation.summary: Sets the animal population: whether it runs, the most animals, and rules per kind.
setAnimalPopulation.exampleLua: kcds.characters.Npc.setAnimalPopulation({ enabled = true, maxAnimals = 40, kinds = { Wolf = { percent = 50 }, Boar = { respawnMinutes = 20 } } })
setAnimalPopulation.exampleCs: Npc.SetAnimalPopulation(new { enabled = true, maxAnimals = 40, kinds = new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["Wolf"] = new { percent = 50 }, ["Boar"] = new { respawnMinutes = 20 } } });

setAnimalPopulationEnabled.summary: Turns the animal population on or off.

setAnimalSpecies.summary: Sets the rules for one animal class, as a percentage or an options object.
setAnimalSpecies.exampleLua:
local Npc = kcds.characters.Npc

Npc.setAnimalSpecies("Wolf", 50)
Npc.setAnimalSpecies("Raven", { enabled = false })

animalSpots.summary: The game's animal spawn points in a level.

setHarvestTable.summary: Sets what skinning each animal class gives, replacing the game's own yields. Until a resource calls it, a carcass gives what the game gives for that animal (its loot from lootOf, without the trophies and special parts), so gutting works without a table. A class left out gives nothing, and {} turns off gutting for all animals.
setHarvestTable.exampleLua: kcds.characters.Npc.setHarvestTable({ Boar = { { item = "boarMeat", amount = 2 } }, RedDeerStag = { { item = "deerMeat", amount = 3 } } })
setHarvestTable.exampleCs: Npc.SetHarvestTable(new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["Boar"] = new object[] { new { item = "boarMeat", amount = 2 } }, ["RedDeerStag"] = new object[] { new { item = "deerMeat", amount = 3 } } });

harvestTable.summary: The current harvest table, {} until a resource sets one (the game's own yields apply then).

appearance.summary: Its character parts: { body, head, hair, beard }.

setCombatSkill.summary: Sets how often it parries and how hard it hits. null restores the game's fighting.

outfit.summary: The pieces from setOutfit's list, or null if it wears its soul's clothes.
outfit.exampleLua:
if npc.outfit == nil then
  print(tostring(npc.name) .. " wears its soul's clothes")
end

wear.summary: Makes it wear these item classes, by name or GUID from Inventory.classes.

setOutfit.summary: Dresses it in one of the game's outfits, by a name or GUID from Player.outfitSets, returning true if its gender has one by that name. Or it takes a list of item classes, each by name, id or { item, quality, health }. It then wears and holds exactly these, including clothing, armour, weapons, shields and ammunition, on all its bodies, as worn rows of getInventory() replacing those from an earlier setOutfit or wear. Returns true once sent, and throws for an unusable item or if the inventory has no room.
setOutfit.exampleCs:
npc.SetOutfit("_cls2_craftsman_01");
npc.SetOutfit(new object[] { new { item = "longSwordDuel", quality = 3, health = 0.8 } });

lootable.summary: Whether its dead body can be searched.

harvested.summary: Whether its carcass has been skinned.
harvested.exampleLua:
if deer.harvested then
  print("already skinned")
end

harvestable.summary: Whether its carcass can be skinned now.
harvestable.exampleLua:
if deer.harvestable then
  print("ready to skin")
end

brain.summary: Whether the game's brain runs it. When false, it stays put and does not think, perceive or fight on its own.

attackable.summary: False means players cannot fight it. They cannot lock on, and their blows, shots and horses' hits land nowhere, so it does not react and the game sees no attack to punish. It still talks, walks and trades. Also an option of Npc.create. True by default.
attackable.exampleLua:
local shopkeeper = kcds.characters.Npc.create({ soul = "townswoman", position = kcds.math.Vector3.new(100, 200, 25), attackable = false })
print(shopkeeper.attackable)
attackable.exampleCs:
var shopkeeper = Npc.Create(new { soul = "townswoman", position = new Vector3(100, 200, 25), attackable = false });
Log.Info(shopkeeper.Attackable);

targetable.summary: Whether players can lock on to it.

interactable.summary: Whether players can talk to it: false takes the game's Talk, Chat and Reply prompts off its body in every game, and the use key no longer fires npcInteract.

nameShown.summary: Whether the game names it in the bottom right corner of the HUD when a player looks at it, true by default. False leaves the name out in every game; its prompts, such as Talk, stay.
nameShown.example:
// A stranger whose name nobody knows yet.
npc.nameShown = false;
nameShown.exampleLua:
-- A stranger whose name nobody knows yet.
npc.nameShown = false
nameShown.exampleCs:
// A stranger whose name nobody knows yet.
npc.NameShown = false;

simulator.summary: The player whose game runs it, or null.
simulator.exampleLua: print(tostring(npc.name) .. " runs on " .. (npc.simulator and npc.simulator.nickname) or "nobody" .. "'s game")

hold.summary: Drops its order and keeps it still.

moveTo.summary: Walks to a position, with `speed` 'walk', 'jog' or 'run', and `radius`.

patrol.summary: Walks a route or list of points.
patrol.exampleLua:
local Vector3 = kcds.math.Vector3

guard:patrol({ Vector3.new(1650, 2150, 37), Vector3.new(1680, 2150, 37) }, { mode = "pingPong", speed = "walk", waitSeconds = 5 })
patrol.exampleCs: guard.Patrol(new[] { new Vector3(1650, 2150, 37), new Vector3(1680, 2150, 37) }, new { mode = "pingPong", speed = "walk", waitSeconds = 5 });

follow.summary: Trails a player or NPC, 3 m behind by default.

useObject.summary: Sits on a seat or lies on a bed of a SmartObject a script placed, the way the game's own people do: it walks to where the game's own people start sitting down on that side, sits down with the game's own animation and stays seated until stopUsingObject or another order. npcObjectUseStarted follows when it sits, and npcObjectUseEnded when the use ends. Nearby players see it, and so does a player who comes later. A seat takes one NPC at a time. options: place (one of the object's seat places; the first free one by default) and side (where it comes from, such as 'front', 'back', 'left' or 'right'; the seat's first by default). Returns false when no seat is free, the NPC is dead, in another dimension or uses something already, or the seat's approach point is off the map. It also takes one of the level's own seats, beds and work places from SmartObject.levelPlaces (place 0); at a work place it works as the game's people do there (a smith forges at his anvil) until stopUsingObject. Throws TypeError for anything but a placed SmartObject or a level place, or one without a seat or bed, and RangeError for a place or side it does not have.

params.object: A SmartObject from SmartObject.spawn with seats or beds, such as 'Bench/bench_2places_low'.

useObject.example:
const bench = kcds.world.SmartObject.spawn({ blueprint: 'Bench/bench_2places_low', position: [10, 20, 30] });
npc.useObject(bench);
useObject.exampleLua:
local bench = kcds.world.SmartObject.spawn({ blueprint = "Bench/bench_2places_low", position = { 10, 20, 30 } })
npc:useObject(bench)
useObject.exampleCs:
var bench = SmartObject.Spawn(new { blueprint = "Bench/bench_2places_low", position = new[] { 10, 20, 30 } });
npc.UseObject(bench);

stopUsingObject.summary: Stands up from the seat or bed it uses, with the game's own animation, or stops walking there. npcObjectUseEnded follows with 'stopped'. Returns false when it uses nothing.

usingObject.summary: What it uses now: { object, place } from useObject, also while it walks there, or null.
usingObject.exampleLua:
if npc.usingObject then
  print(npc.name .. " sits on " .. npc.usingObject.object.blueprint)
end

lookAt.summary: Turns towards a player, NPC or position.

attack.summary: Fights a living player or NPC within 128 m. `weapon` can select, for example, 'bow'.

params.position: Where to put it, with missing components staying.
params.rotation: Optional: Euler degrees or a Quaternion. With none, it keeps its direction.
